text:
anya: FYI swapped staging -> model-checkpoint-2026-04c at 13:02 UTC and p99 token latency jumped ~45% compared to prior build. looks like tokens/sec drop, not load. (reaction :eyes:)
mike: ugh. did we also change tokenizer shard/normalization in that package?
anya: no tokenizer code in the package — just new checkpoint + config.yaml from model team. but config drift includes token_map_version: v3 and pad_strategy: dynamic.
raj: can you paste a short profiler capture? even a flame or top stacks helps.
anya: pasted below (sampling for 30s on a hot worker):
```
Top op latency (ms):
- attention_kernel_select: 3.2 -> 9.8
- kv_cache_lookup: 0.9 -> 4.1
- batch_scheduler_flush: 1.1 -> 1.3
Hot path: kernel selection spends more time probing alternative kernels per sequence length.
KV misses up from 7% -> 28% on same workload (likely changed kvkey distribution from tokenizer tweak).
```
carmen: interesting — kernel selector is spending extra cycles due to sequence length histogram skew? Any change in prompt framing in checkpoint inference config?
anya: model config now sets default_max_len: 2048 and sends longer prefills in some eval routes. previously we had 1024 default. but workloads mostly same, so suspect tokenizer produces longer tokenized sequences for short inputs.
mike: that maps to kernel heuristics: we pick different matmul kernels if seq_len > threshold. if many more sequences cross threshold, we recompile/select slower kernels.
raj: propose a quick bisect plan: revert to previous checkpoint on one staging pool and see if p99 drops. if yes, we can confirm checkpoint change is root cause.
anya: started a canary revert on pool-stg-a at 13:16 UTC: `deploy rollback --pool pool-stg-a --to model-checkpoint-2026-03b`. will report in ~5m.
slo-bot: Alert: p99 latency (pool-stg-a) decreased 42% after rollback to model-checkpoint-2026-03b.
mike: that's a clear signal. next: we should capture KV key distribution from both checkpoints and tokenizer outputs for a few sample inputs. raj, can you add a lightweight probe in the staging runtime to log hashed kv keys histogram? low overhead.
raj: on it. adding `kvcache_probe: hist(v=hash_prefix, bins=128)` to runtime on pool-stg-b. will collect 1 min.
anya: probe shows hash_prefix concentrated in the high range for new checkpoint (v3 map) -> uneven shard hotness and more evictions; also tokenization lengths shifted +14% p50.
mike: two orthogonal problems: (1) tokenizer mapping changed key distribution -> kvcache thrash, (2) sequence length shift -> kernel selection hot-swap. Both amplify p99.
carmen: for immediate mitigation we can: 1) revert checkpoint on staging/rollout pause 2) pin tokenizer map to v2 for canary/pipelines 3) add kernel selection short-circuit for small deltas (avoid full probe on first few requests). which to do now?
anya: we've paused the rollout and rolled pool-stg-a back. I'll open a PR to pin tokenizer map in the model registry to v2 for the next deploy.
mike: meanwhile i'll add a fast-path heuristic: if seq_len change < 20% compared to cached hist for that route, skip heavy kernel probe for first N windows. cheap fix and reversible.
raj: implementing kvcache pre-warm for new key prefixes in onboarding flow might reduce thrash during shadow rollouts. propose pre-warm script that touches top-5 prefixes per checkpoint during deploy.
carmen: good idea. also we should add a CI perf test: on any model-onboard PR, run microbench with synthetic prompts to assert p99 doesn't exceed baseline +15% and kv_miss_rate < 12%.
anya: creating a perf-gate issue: `perf/onboard: add p99 and kvcache gating for model registries`. linking in the PR.
infra-bot: Note: created alert `staging.p99.model_onboard_regression` with threshold 1.35x baseline.
mike: final action items: (1) pause rollout (done), (2) revert canary (done), (3) add kvcache hist capture + pre-warm (raj), (4) fast-path kernel probe short-circuit (mike), (5) CI perf gating + pin tokenizer map for pipeline (anya/carmen). I'll draft rollout resume checklist after tests.
anya: will follow up with a short postmortem once mitigations are validated. thanks all.
mike: thx — saved a regen deploy until we have CI gate and pre-warm. :thumbsup:
